parameters.content:
## Shopify collections SEO

Finds the collections your catalogue can support and shoppers search for, asks you in Slack, then creates them as smart collections. Gives every brand its own page and proposes unpublishing collections that run out of stock.

### How it works
1. **Setup** (run once) creates the `collection_proposals` Supabase table.
2. **Propose** (weekly) groups live products by product type and metafield value, and by brand and type, names each group with AI, checks Google search volume, difficulty and whether you already rank, scores it, and posts the best to Slack.
3. **Review** (Slack buttons) checks Slack's signature and records Approve or Skip.
4. **Apply** creates, unpublishes or republishes the collection in Shopify and replies on the card.
5. **Brands** (daily) creates a collection for every new vendor.
6. **Retire** (weekly) proposes unpublishing collections this template made that fall below `retire_below` live products, and republishing them when stock returns.

### Setup
1. Credentials: Postgres with your Supabase connection string on every table node, Custom Auth with your Shopify client ID and secret on every **Get Shopify token** node, Slack API on the Slack nodes, Crypto with your Slack signing secret on **Sign the request**, Basic Auth with your DataForSEO login on the three DataForSEO nodes, Ollama on **Ollama Chat Model**.
2. Fill in each lane's settings node.
3. Run **Run once to set up**.
4. Point your Slack app's Interactivity URL at **Slack button click**, then publish.

### Customisation
- Swap **Ollama Chat Model** for any chat model sub-node.
- Set `review_brands` to true to get a card for each brand.
- Raise or lower `create_score` once you trust the cards.

## Setup (run once)
Creates the `collection_proposals` Supabase table. Safe to run again: an existing table is kept.

parameters.query:
create table if not exists collection_proposals (
  id integer generated by default as identity primary key,
  key text,
  kind text,
  source text,
  product_type text,
  vendor text,
  attr_key text,
  attr_value text,
  raw_title text,
  title text,
  handle text,
  keywords text,
  main_keyword text,
  volume double precision,
  live_count double precision,
  score double precision,
  floor double precision,
  sample_titles text,
  rule_set text,
  name_source text,
  skip_reason text,
  status text,
  collection_id text,
  slack_channel text,
  slack_ts text,
  error text,
  "createdAt" timestamptz not null default now(),
  "updatedAt" timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (key)
);

parameters.text:
=You name a collection page for an online store.

Category: {{ $json.product_type }}
Attribute: {{ $json.attr_label || 'brand' }}
Value: {{ $json.attr_value || $json.vendor }}
Brand for this page: {{ $json.source === 'brand_type' ? $json.vendor : 'none' }}
Products on the page: {{ $json.live_count }}
Sample product titles:
{{ $json.sample_titles.join('\n') }}
Existing collections in this category:
{{ $json.sibling_titles.join('\n') || 'none' }}

Title:
- The words a shopper would type to find these products, in Title Case, plural.
- Value first, category noun last.
- Units as shoppers write them: 8 Port, 4K, 2TB, 5m.
- Name a brand only if "Brand for this page" is not none, spelled exactly as given.
- No model numbers. No product names. No claims such as best or cheap.
- 60 characters or fewer.

Keywords:
- 3 to 8 phrases a shopper would type into Google to find this page.
- Lower case.
- Every phrase contains the value or the brand.
- No model numbers.

skip_reason:
- Explain in a few words when the value only works as a filter, not a page: pack quantities, internal codes, materials shoppers don't search for.
- Explain when the page would repeat an existing collection.
- Otherwise an empty string.

Reply with only this JSON object: {"title": "...", "keywords": ["..."], "skip_reason": ""}

nodes.notes: Ollama Cloud: an Ollama credential with Base URL https://ollama.com and your API key. Swap for any chat model.

nodes.name: Search volume
nodes.notes: DataForSEO: one task for every keyword, about US$0.09.
